title: RNA to Amino Acids (Translation)
summary: Students divide a six-base RNA sequence into two codons and read each one against the codon chart, building a two-amino-acid chain and meeting the start and stop codons.
outcomes: Divide an RNA sequence into codons (groups of three bases).
Use a codon chart to determine which amino acids correspond to each codon.
Explain the role of the start codon (AUG) and stop codons in translation.
Understand how proteins are built one amino acid at a time.
